paper.central_claim: An autoresearch loop can be used to improve itself: an outer loop that reads the inner loop's code and trace and generates/injects new search mechanisms as Python code at runtime (Level 2) yields a 5x larger val_bpb improvement than the inner loop alone on Karpathy's GPT pretraining benchmark (-0.045 vs -0.009), whereas parameter-level adjustment (Level 1.5) gives no reliable gain; this is a first bilevel step toward recursive bootstrapping.
paper.title: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself

evidence.quote: iterations 4–30 repeat these same two changes, accumulating up to 22 consecutive discards.
evidence.support_explanation: Evidence of the bottleneck: baseline inner loop repeats proposals deterministically.

evidence.quote: Group B’s outer loop freezes TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE after the failed increase, blocking the decrease direction entirely.
evidence.support_explanation: Explains why parameter-level adjustment (Level 1.5) did not help: it froze the productive direction.

evidence.quote: Five of six generated code artifacts passed import validation and were activated; one primary mechanism (GP Regressor) was reverted due to a missing sklearn dependency.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism generation succeeded at first attempt; one of the primary mechanisms was reverted for a missing dependency.

evidence.quote: Three repeats per group is insufficient for rigorous statistical comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede n = 3 is inadequate; Group C SD is 67% of mean.

evidence.quote: All results are on one task: GPT pretraining at 50M parameters with a 300-second budget on RTX 5090.
evidence.support_explanation: Single task, single hardware, single LLM (DeepSeek deepseek-chat).

evidence.quote: each Level 2 research session adds approximately 3 minutes of wall time and four additional LLM calls.
evidence.support_explanation: Outer-loop overhead reported qualitatively per session; total tokens and wall-clock per group not tabulated.

evidence.quote: Because our experimental budget fixes the number of inner iterations rather than total wall-clock time, this overhead does not reduce the number of inner evaluations; it should instead be interpreted as an additional cost of the bilevel architecture.
evidence.support_explanation: Groups are matched on inner iterations, not on total compute; Group A is not given the outer-loop budget.

evidence.quote: A preliminary run was invalidated because the Level 2 dynamic loading pipeline contained a sys.modules registration bug, causing all mechanism injections to silently fall back to the original runner.
evidence.support_explanation: Disclosed failed run and the fragility of silent fallback; supports honesty but also shows injection can silently not apply.

evidence.quote: They do not demonstrate unbounded recursive self-improvement or prove that mechanisms discovered for Level 1 will improve Level 2.
evidence.support_explanation: Recursive claim is explicitly out of scope; only outer-improves-inner is tested.

evidence.quote: Whether Level 2 would discover equally effective—or entirely different—mechanisms under an unconstrained prompt remains untested.
evidence.support_explanation: Level 2 prompt names candidate domains; mechanism discovery is steered by the prompt author.

evidence.quote: We are not aware of earlier autoresearch systems in which an autonomous outer loop writes and injects code that modifies the structural logic of the inner autoresearch loop at runtime, using the same model that runs the inner loop.
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim is scoped to autoresearch systems; self-modifying agent frameworks are outside the stated lineage.

evidence.quote: Level 2 was not told which specific mechanism to implement, though the prompt suggested broad neighboring domains.
evidence.support_explanation: Mechanism domain (tabu, bandit, DOE) is partly prompted by neighbouring-domain suggestions.

evidence.quote: Level 2 executes every 2 outer cycles.
evidence.support_explanation: Two Level 2 sessions per repeat in the 30-iteration budget (six sessions in Group C).

evidence.quote: Group C’s separation from Groups A and B provides evidence that Level 2 mechanism injection is the primary driver in the full bilevel setting.
evidence.support_explanation: Author interpretation; conflicts in part with the Group D confound (E010) and with n = 3.

evidence.quote: All levels use the same DeepSeek deepseek-chat model.
evidence.support_explanation: No stronger model at the meta level; one backbone only.

Our reading of the Related Work: the autoresearch lineage, FunSearch/algorithm design, ADOPT, PiEvo and later concurrent works are discussed, while earlier self-modifying agent frameworks that edit their own improvement code (e.g., Godel Agent, Darwin Godel Machine, ADAS) are not cited in the text provided.

evidence.quote: The LLM, given the same state, generates nearly the same proposals every time.
evidence.support_explanation: The baseline proposer is near-deterministic. The obvious naive fix (temperature/seed diversity, restarts or a hand-coded tabu list) is never run, although Level 2's winning mechanisms are exactly such diversifiers.

evidence.quote: However, the per-repeat reports show that Group D’s generated mechanism patches were not successfully applied or validated
evidence.support_explanation: Two of three Group D repeats reach −0.063/−0.039 with no applied mechanism, so the decisive batch-size move occurs without successful injection.

evidence.quote: Baseline val_bpb varies slightly across repeats due to training randomness (range 1.094–1.114).
evidence.support_explanation: The 0.02 baseline spread exceeds Groups A/B's gains (0.006–0.009); a single 300-s evaluation's noise floor is never measured.

evidence.quote: We are not aware of earlier autoresearch systems in which an autonomous outer loop writes and injects code that modifies the structural logic of the inner autoresearch loop at runtime
evidence.support_explanation: The novelty claim is scoped to 'autoresearch systems'. Self-referential improvers that edit their own improvement code (Gödel Agent, DGM, ADAS) do not appear in §2.

gap.author_gap: Autoresearch systems (Karpathy single-track, AutoResearchClaw multi-batch, EvoScientist persistent memory) have human-designed search procedures; no system lets the loop discover or replace that procedure.
gap.checked_gap: The residue is real and evidenced in this setting: the baseline loop repeats the same two proposals for iterations 4-30 and misses the batch-size direction. The nearest neighbors for self-editing improvement code (Godel Agent, DGM, ADAS and similar) are not covered in the stated lineage, so the novelty claim is scoped to autoresearch systems.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Autoresearch lineage (Karpathy 2026, AutoResearchClaw, EvoScientist); FunSearch/LLM algorithm design; ADOPT and PiEvo; later concurrent works Meta-Harness, GEAR, AEvo etc. added in v2 as complementary.
gap.residue: Whether mechanisms transfer across seeds, tasks and hardware; whether the outer loop can itself be improved.
gap.stakes: Search deadlock in LLM-driven hyperparameter optimization.
gap.method_response: Outer LLM session writes new search code injected at runtime.
gap.remaining_gap: Attribution to injected mechanisms, generality, recursion, compute-matched comparison.
unresolved: Overlap with self-referential coding-agent frameworks not cited

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On one 50M-parameter pretraining benchmark on one GPU with one LLM, runs that included a code-generating outer loop reached a markedly better val_bpb than plain or parameter-tuned inner loops in 2 of 3 repeats (selected and reported on the same metric); injection of the generated mechanisms as the cause is not established because the injection-only group's patches were not applied.
unresolved: Attribution of gains to injected mechanisms
Opus: no naive diversification baseline for a near-deterministic proposer (opus:O01).
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; nothing was run by us. Central claim retained as stated; supported conclusion is narrower.
assessment.evidence_level_note: The edited object is the inner improver, and C vs A/B compares mechanism-on with mechanism-off at equal inner evaluations. But selection and report share val_bpb (EVIDENCE rule 2), and Group D's gains without applied mechanisms leave the improved mechanism's causal role open, so not 'improver' or 'retained'.

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. The residue is evidenced (Group A repeats the same two proposals for iterations 4–30), but the closest lineage (self-referential agents that edit their own improvement code: Gödel Agent, DGM, ADAS) is absent, and novelty is scoped to 'autoresearch systems' (opus:O04). Anchor 2: neighbour comparison incomplete.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The two-level design and the stated hypotheses (L1.5 vs L2) are reconstructible. But the diagnosed bottleneck is a proposer that 'generates nearly the same proposals every time' (opus:O01), and the winning generated mechanisms are standard diversifiers. No prediction separates LLM-generated mechanisms from directly diversifying the proposer, and L1.5, the only stated contrast, is a freeze rule that the paper shows blocks the decisive direction.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Algorithm 1, periods and the 4-call dialogue are reproducible. Retention is import-validated only (no performance gate or retirement), the anchor is unnamed, Group D patches failed to apply, and a silent-fallback bug invalidated a preliminary run.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with sol. val_bpb on a fixed validation split is a credible metric for this task, and absolute Δ values are reported per repeat. son55's two grounds, small gains below the baseline spread and the metric doubling as selection criterion, are a noise defect (E.statistics) and a selection defect (E.holdout), charged there (A2). Not 4: the '5×' is a ratio of improvement magnitudes, and the per-evaluation noise floor is unmeasured (opus:O03).

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The four-group level ablation holds model, GPU, training budget and inner evaluations fixed, and C separates from A/B. But Group D reaches the same batch-size move without applied mechanisms (opus:O02), individual mechanisms are not ablated, no naive diversification baseline exists (opus:O01), and outer LLM calls are unmatched (A2).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 0 (sol resolved, son55 not_reported; Opus keeps resolved, since the zero rests on reported design facts). The keep/discard metric is the reported metric, best configurations are not re-evaluated, there is one task/GPU/LLM, and mechanism transfer is future work.

E.statistics.reason: Opus sides with sol (A2 ladder). Three repeats per group with per-repeat values and mean±SD give cross-run variance, beyond the ladder-2 description; no interval or test, n=3 that the authors call insufficient, and an uncontrolled baseline spread (opus:O03) keep it below 3. son55's 1 fits 'main result without uncertainty', but the SD is reported.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Outer overhead per session is quantified (≈3 min, 4 LLM calls), and inner evaluations are matched with the non-parity stated. No total tokens or wall-clock per group.
